chunk_findings.detail: The `_PYTEST` pattern is not anchored to pytest’s temp root; its optional prefix consumes any preceding non-whitespace path. Given `digest("/repo/a/pytest-of-user/pytest-0/test.py")` and `digest("/repo/b/pytest-of-user/pytest-0/test.py")`, both normalise to `<pytest-tmp>/test.py`, so the digests are equal even though the repo-relative paths differ. That can hide a new failure whose only difference is a directory above a `pytest-of-*/pytest-*` component, contradicting the promise that a different repo-relative path still differs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/failure_text.py:26

chunk_findings.detail: `normalise` replaces named roots with plain `str.replace` without requiring a path-component boundary. Given `normalise("[REDACTED:path]", ["[REDACTED:path]"])`, it returns `<tree>-old/test.py`, although `[REDACTED:path]` is outside the named root and the docstring says a path outside any tree is left alone. If baseline compare passes a tree root and failure text mentions a sibling path with that prefix, the sibling is corrupted/misclassified as inside the tree.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/failure_text.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: The help topic says failures are rewritten “before two failures are compared by digest”, but the whole change only adds the helper and tests; no baseline-compare call site is changed to use `failure_text.normalise` or `failure_text.digest`. For a base failure text `/tmp/ddflow-base.abc/tests/test.py` and a candidate failure text `[REDACTED:path]`, the unchanged baseline compare still digests the raw strings and sees two failures; the documented normalisation does not actually happen.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/gates.md:58

chunk_findings.detail: The help says a pytest temp directory is rewritten to `<tree>`, but the code uses `PYTEST_TMP = "<pytest-tmp>"` and `_PYTEST.sub(PYTEST_TMP, ...)`. For example, `normalise("/tmp/pytest-of-user/pytest-0/test.py")` returns `<pytest-tmp>/test.py`, not `<tree>/test.py`, so the documented placeholder is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/gates.md:59

chunk_findings.detail: This test only checks that two messages differing in `/tmp/pytest-of-<user>/pytest-<n>` have the same digest; it never checks that the text after the pytest temp root survives normalisation. A `normalise` implementation whose pytest pattern blanks the rest of the line (for example `re.sub(r"/tmp/pytest-of-.*", "<tree>", text)`) passes this test and all other shown tests, but would give the same digest to `boom /tmp/pytest-of-ana/pytest-17/test_a0/x.txt` and `boom /tmp/pytest-of-bob/pytest-3/test_a0/y.txt` (or different text after the temp path), suppressing a real new failure. The suite therefore does not keep the acceptance that a real new message still differs for pytest-temp failure text.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_failure_text_paths.py:test_pytest_temp_dirs_are_blanked

chunk_findings.detail: The test guards only against a shorter root being replaced before a child root (`/srv/ci/run/7` before `/srv/ci/run/7/sub`). It does not guard against replacing a root that is merely a textual prefix of a different path component. A minimal `text.replace(root, "<tree>")` implementation passes every shown test, but with `roots=["/srv/ci/run/7"]` and failure text containing `/srv/ci/run/77/tests/data/x.json` it produces `<tree>7/tests/data/x.json`, corrupting an unrelated path and potentially making different failures compare incorrectly. The suite therefore permits a wrong boundary-handling implementation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_failure_text_paths.py:test_a_named_root_is_blanked_too_longest_first

chunk_findings.detail: `str.replace` is not a path-boundary check, so a named root that is a string prefix of a different path is rewritten anyway. `normalise("/srv/ci/run/70/tests/data/x.json", ["/srv/ci/run/7"])` returns `"<tree>0/tests/data/x.json"`. That path is not under `/srv/ci/run/7`, contradicting the claim that a path outside any tree is left alone. The same corruption makes unrelated failures share a digest: `digest("/srv/ci/run/70/same.txt", ["/srv/ci/run/7"])` equals `digest("/other/0/same.txt", ["/other"])` because both become `"<tree>0/same.txt"`. Baseline compare can then treat a new cause as the old red. Longest-first sorting does not help; `/srv/ci/run/70` is not a longer registered root.

chunk_findings.detail: This test only checks that two base/worktree variants have the same digest; it does not check that a different message or repo-relative path under those same tree roots still differs. A `normalise` implementation that rewrites the whole tail after a base tree path, e.g. `/tmp/ddflow-base.<id>.*` to `<tree>` (and similarly for the worktree root), passes all shown tests because the “real new message” and “different repo-relative path” tests use `/tmp/ddflow-ci.aaaa`, not `/tmp/ddflow-base.abc123` or the worktree root. That implementation would incorrectly give the same digest to `/tmp/ddflow-base.abc123/tests/data/x.json not found` and `/tmp/ddflow-base.abc123/tests/data/y.json not found`, violating the promise that a real new message still differs for base-tree failures.

Distinct non-tree paths then share a digest: `digest("E /opt/ddflow-ci.abc-extra/f")` equals `digest("E /opt/ddflow-base.zzz-extra/f")`.

chunk_findings.detail: Named roots are substituted sequentially against the already-substituted text, so an earlier replacement can remove the `/` that originally prevented `_START` from matching an internal path component. For example, `normalise("/a/b/f", ["/a", "/b"])` first replaces `/a`, producing `<tree>/b/f`, then replaces `/b`, producing `<tree><tree>/f`. The same result is produced by `normalise("/b/a/f", ["/a", "/b"])`, so `digest` collapses two different repo-relative paths (`b/f` under `/a` vs `a/f` under `/b`) to one digest. Sorting by length/name makes the result deterministic but does not make it correct.

chunk_findings.detail: `_END` only treats `/`, whitespace, `:`, quotes, `)`, `]`, `,`, or EOS as a path boundary, so a tree path that ends a sentence is not a root. `normalise("Error: /tmp/ddflow-base.aaa111.")` and `normalise("Error: /tmp/ddflow-ci.bbb222.")` both stay unchanged because `.` is not in `_END` and is not part of the id class, so `digest` differs for the same failure and an old red still looks new.
